correctness.rationale: The constant Neumann subspace solves exactly the planar equations for all d1,d2, and its periodic solutions therefore occur at the same a values with or without diffusion. For sigma=1 the positive equilibrium is (1/sqrt(a),(sqrt(a)-1)/a); the kinetic trace 1-2/sqrt(a) gives crossing speed 1/16 at a=4. The Jacobian at (1/2,1/4) has rows (-1/2,-3/2) and (1/2,1/2), and frequency omega=1/sqrt(2). For a direct planar normal-form check set X=V-1/4 and Y=-(U-1/2+V-1/4)/sqrt(2). Then the canonical linear part is (-omega Y,omega X) and the nonlinear terms are F=-X^2-3sqrt(2)XY-4X^3-4sqrt(2)X^2Y and G=(X+sqrt(2)Y)^2/sqrt(2). The planar cubic radial formula gives -24/16+2sqrt(2)/(16omega)=-5/4 in physical time and this real linear amplitude. The convention in the checker has X=2 Re z to first order and scales time by omega, giving 4(-5/4)/omega=-5sqrt(2). The negative coefficient and positive crossing put the small homogeneous cycles at a>4. In the H1 criteria as recorded, the ratio 5/2 lies between 1^2 and 2^2 and substitution gives r1=2<10. For mode 1 the matrix is the kinetic Jacobian minus diag(10,1/5), with trace -51/5 and determinant -12/5. Its positive simple eigenvalue gives a limiting Floquet multiplier >1 and persists by continuity for small homogeneous cycles; modes k>=2 have positive determinants 1/2-(49/10)k^2+2k^4 and negative traces. This independently establishes the branch side, transverse instability, and the contradiction with positive determinants if the primary assertion is as reported.
